The visuals were captured by Marcio Amaro and photographer Andrés, known as andreslpaez.

items.title: After 24 years together, woman loses home to partner's estranged wife
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: Dimica Hicks, who lived in a Phoenix house with her partner Troy Torrence for 24 years, has lost her claim to the property after his death. An Arizona appeals court upheld ownership rights of Torrence's estranged wife, Rita Mack, who had moved out in 1999 but remained legally married to him. The court ruled that Mack inherited the house under their joint ownership agreement, while rejecting Hicks's claims based on her long stay and contributions towards the property.

items.description: Recent excavations at Sutton Hoo have revealed a unique 'sand body' along with various grave goods. items.title: Why you keep checking your phone for social media notifications that never come
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: The prevalence of smartphones has fostered a compulsive behavior where users check their devices even in the absence of alerts. Implementing small changes, like disabling unnecessary notifications, can effectively disrupt this routine behavior.

items.title: New Jersey mother, son sue zoning board over rejected bayfront home plan
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: A New Jersey mother and her son have approached the court after a township zoning board rejected their plan to build a three-storey house on their bayfront plot. They argue that the board failed to properly consider expert evidence and the property's existing limitations. The family wants the rejection overturned and has also sought compensation, claiming that the decision effectively deprives them of the use of their land.

items.title: Bihar porter sells family land to fund sons' education; both secure admissions
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: Manoj Kumar, a porter in Gaya's bustling grain market, made tremendous sacrifices to foster his sons' educational dreams. By selling a family farm plot, he ensured they could attend coaching in Kota. The outcome was worth it: Sonu scored a commendable 636 in NEET UG 2026, leading to his CAPFIMS admission, while Monu's impressive 93 percentile in JEE Main 2026 secured him a place at BIT Mesra for Chemical Engineering.

items.title: Colleen Begg is the first woman to win Prince William’s Tusk lifetime award
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: Dr. Colleen Begg has earned the prestigious 2026 Prince William Award due to her remarkable contributions to wildlife conservation in Mozambique. Initially researching honey badgers, she then redirected her passion towards safeguarding lions and other carnivores. Together with her husband, they launched the Niassa Carnivore Project, promoting local community involvement and empowering women in Africa's environmental leadership.

items.title: In a first, credit card spends pip ATM withdrawals
items.author: MAYUR SHETTY
items.description: In a significant milestone for India’s financial landscape, October 2026 marked the first month where credit card spending overtook ATM withdrawals. With credit card transactions soaring to over Rs 2.4 lakh crore compared to Rs 2.3 lakh crore in ATM withdrawals, this evolution underscores changing consumer preferences. Remarkably, credit card spending saw a year-on-year increase of 14.4 percent, highlighting a shift that began back in November 2019.

items.title: Tata, Hyundai, Audi to raise prices on higher input costs
items.author: AABHAS SHARMA
items.description: Starting in December, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles and Hyundai Motor India will implement price hikes, echoing similar moves by Maruti Suzuki amid escalating commodity costs. Tata anticipates a modest increase of about 0.5 percent, while Hyundai may raise some model prices by up to Rs 8,000. Despite lower passenger vehicle registrations, the industry experienced varied success during the festive season, with overall vehicle retail remaining relatively strong.

items.title: Study of 18,457 skeletons finds men in Southeast Asia lost 7 inches in height
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: Innovative farming technologies have surprisingly led to a decrease in human height over millennia, as revealed by research analyzing thousands of skeletal remains. This shift might be attributed to heightened population density, which adversely affected nutrition and health, thereby altering growth trends across different regions.

items.author: TNN
items.description: National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Maldives defense minister Hassan Rasheed discussed security cooperation at the Colombo Security Conclave. This meeting marked the first high-level interaction between the two countries since President Mohamed Muizzu's recent visit to Pakistan. During that visit, Maldives signed 20 agreements with Pakistan related to defense and maritime issues. Additionally, Muizzu called for resuming the Saarc summit process to enhance regional cooperation.

items.title: Utah banker mailed 37 tons of bricks to build a bank, forcing postal rule changes
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: In 1916, the directors of the Bank of Vernal needed bricks for a new building project. They faced high transportation costs due to poor road conditions in rural Utah. A director discovered that shipping bricks by postal service was a cheaper option, allowing many small packages to be sent. This unique approach led to changes in postal regulations regarding large shipments.

items.title: Scientists discover 5-million-year-old coral atoll hidden 900 metres underwater
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: A groundbreaking expedition has unveiled a submerged coral atoll in the Romanche Fracture Zone that dates back five million years. This undersea marvel is home to exquisite sponge gardens and ancient corals that are around 1,000 years old. Scientists have explored ecosystems at depths ranging from 600 to 4,300 metres, revealing significant ecological value and potential contributions to marine conservation under the High Seas Treaty.

items.title: Around 1,000 books, 3 libraries: How Telangana police are helping tribal job aspirants
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: In a commendable effort to enhance educational resources, Adilabad police have launched three new libraries in tribal villages, providing crucial exam preparation materials. With approximately 1,000 books tailored for various government recruitment exams, including UPSC and DSC, local gram panchayats partnered with the police to create these facilities. This initiative aims to empower local youth in their pursuit of government jobs, eliminating the need for extensive travel.

items.title: India’s space economy projected to rise to $40-45 billion by 2036: Science minister
items.author: SURENDRA SINGH
items.description: India's space economy is expected to significantly increase, rising from nearly $9 billion to $40-45 billion by 2036. This growth will largely be driven by private companies contributing to the space sector. Space, Science and Technology Minister Jitendra Singh highlighted key reforms that spurred this transformation, including the establishment of New Space India Limited.
